newsitem.title: UK: Energy Grp firm as bid referral fears ease.
newsitem.headline: Energy Grp firm as bid referral fears ease.

text.p: Shares in Energy Group Plc rose in a mostly weak UK equity market on Monday as press reports eased fears the government could block PacifiCorp's 696p-per-share takeover bid, dealers said.
Energy shares were up 1-1/2p at 647-1/2 by 0858 GMT in thin volume of 164,255 shares, even as the FTSE 100 index traded 28.8 points lower at 4,754.3.
The Lex column in Saturday's Financial Times said Energy Group shares looked cheap and that the bid should be approved since it raised no competition concerns.
"At a 50p discount to the offer, EG shares look close to a one-way bet," the column said.

Separately the Observer newspaper said energy minister John Battle said he was not opposed to foreign ownership of British power companies and was more concerned about ensuring a secure and diverse supply of energy in Britain.
The paper said Battle's comments would likely ease concern that the bid would be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
Energy shares have traded at a wide discount to the bid amid fears that the Labour government, whose takeover policy is as yet untested, could block the move.
